title: Simple Calculator
description: Build arithmetic functions step by step — from basic addition to exponentiation with the ** operator.

steps.title: Add two numbers
steps.description: Write an `add` function that takes two numbers and returns their sum.
hints: The + operator adds two numbers together
Use `return` to send back the result

steps.title: Subtract and multiply
steps.description: Create `subtract` and `multiply` functions. Then test all three operations.
hints: Use - for subtraction and * for multiplication
Keep the same function pattern as add()

verification.failureMessage: Check each function: add(10,5)=15, subtract(10,5)=5, multiply(10,5)=50

steps.title: Divide safely
steps.description: Create a `divide` function that checks for division by zero. If the divisor is 0, return `"Cannot divide by zero"`.
hints: Use an if statement to check if b === 0
Return the error message string when b is 0

verification.successMessage: Safe division — you handled the edge case!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure divide(10,2) returns 5 and divide(10,0) returns the error message.

steps.title: Build a calculator dispatcher
steps.description: Create a `calculate` function that takes an operator string (`'+'`, `'-'`, `'*'`, `'/'`) and two numbers, then calls the right function.
hints: Use a switch statement or if/else chain to check the operator
Call the appropriate function and return its result

def subtract(a, b): return a - b

steps.title: Add exponentiation
steps.description: Extend the calculator with a `power` function using the `**` operator. Add `'^'` support to the dispatcher.
hints: The exponentiation operator is **: a ** b means a raised to the power b
Add a new case for '^' in your switch/if chain

verification.successMessage: Exponentiation works! Your calculator is complete.
